Adding a technical sketch here that we can send to Meridian as a one-pager. I'll attach a short PDF (redwood_sdk_auth_playbook.pdf) and paste the relevant excerpts below. Feedback welcome — I'll iterate before sending externally.

--- excerpt start ---
Auth options (recommended for POC):
- Short-lived API keys (recommended): Redwood token issuer issues keys with TTL 1h, client exchanges a long-lived service credential for ephemeral key via a server-side call. SDK supports a refresh handler (callback) to re-request ephemeral tokens.
- OAuth2: supported for full platform integrations where Meridian needs user-level scopes. Not required for POC.

Streaming semantics (suggested contract):
- Event model: 'open' -> multiple 'delta' events (payload: {token_text, partial_output, kv_state_id?}) -> 'done' event with final token indices and stable output.
- Tool calling while streaming: SDK can emit tool-call placeholders as 'delta' events (partial JSON). We recommend delimiting tool-call boundaries with a special token to avoid JSON streaming parse issues (e.g., '###TOOL-START' / '###TOOL-END'). Client libraries include a streaming JSON assembler to reconstruct tool payloads reliably.

Chat vs completions (tokenization & stop semantics):
- Chat (structured messages): token counting includes role tokens + separators. Stop sequences are applied to the final assembled assistant message. For streaming, partial deltas may not respect stop sequences until the 'done' event; clients should implement local heuristics for early truncation when stop tokens are emitted in deltas.
- Completions (single prompt): simpler token model; stop is applied server-side and attempts to end generation. Streaming sends token deltas identical to the final output tokens.

Billing notes: streaming is billed per emitted token; partial tokens and final tokens are deduplicated by token index for the same request.
--- excerpt end ---

Attachment: redwood_sdk_auth_playbook.pdf

I can convert the excerpt into a short 'streaming contract' JSON schema if we want to push it to them tomorrow.

— Ben
